messages:
raj_infra: Heads up — eu-west GPU capacity exhausted around 08:12 UTC, research sweep kicked off a bunch of long-running jobs and the autoscaler didn't add nodes :rotating_light:
oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-314 created by raj_infra at 08:13 UTC
emma_sre: I see a flurry of Pending pods with 0/4 nodes matching gpu=true taint tolerated
jasper_research: yep, our sweep spawned ~120 jobs, many with preemptible/low priority. Sorry, we should have staggered them.
raj_infra: cloud provider API returned 429s during the peak, looks like throttling. cluster-autoscaler logged repeated scale-up errors: 
```
I1208 08:13:22 scaler.go:345] Failed to scale up: cloudprovider RateLimitExceeded: Too many requests
```
jun_ops: Quickly did an emergency scale — created nodepool gpu-fallback-ephemeral and forced 8 nodes, some came up NotReady then Ready; now kernels got stuck on one node.
jun_ops: kubectl output snip:
```
NAME                                     STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
ip-10-0-45-12.ec2.internal               NotReady   <none>   3m    v1.26.3
ip-10-0-46-98.ec2.internal               Ready      <none>   5m    v1.26.3
```
raj_infra: NotReady nodes had NV driver crash / kubelet restart loop, likely from an older driver on the AMI we used for fallback pool.
emma_sre: Took one NotReady node and checked dmesg: repeated GPU driver OOM and GPU timeout. Rolling back cordon + drain on that node was noisy.
jasper_research: Can we preempt low-priority sweep jobs to free up GPUs? They'll restart later.
jun_ops: I applied a lower priority admission for research jobs, added --evict-unused-gpus flag to the scheduler on a temporary basis. Also scaled down a few idle dev jobs.
raj_infra: Temporary mitigations: 1) scaled fallback pool to 12 with correct AMI; 2) enabled fallback to cpu for jobs that declare gpu: optional; 3) increased cloud API backoff to avoid 429 retry storms.
liz_product: Any customer-facing impact? Observability shows increased latency on hosted endpoints for a few minutes but nothing crossing SLOs. Logged anomalies to the console.
tariq_eng: We should add fairshare enforcement and per-team concurrent GPU quotas so a single sweep can't monopolize. Also queue admission to spread across AZs.
emma_sre: Agreed. Immediate followups: ticket INF-2026-432 to add pre-scale check (if cloud rate limit > X, stagger launches), INF-2026-433 for fairshare quota, INF-2026-434 to bake correct GPU drivers into fallback AMIs.
raj_infra: Will also add a short-circuit in autoscaler to prefer spinning up dedicated reserved pools for high-priority routes before exhausting shared pools.
jasper_research: We're pausing the remainder of the sweep and will resubmit as batched groups of 10. Sorry for the chaos.
jun_ops: Postmortem plan: timeline, root cause (throttled cloud API + wrong AMI + no fairshare), mitigations (backoff, AMI bake, quotas), action owners assigned in INF tickets. I'll own the AMI bake.
emma_sre: Adding a runbook step: if autoscaler returns >3 rate-limit errors in 2m, escalate to infra and create ephemeral fallback with validated AMI.
raj_infra: Thanks — I'll follow up with a change request to cluster-autoscaler flags and a small PR to admission controller to enforce per-team caps. Will update INC-2026-314 when done. :thumbsup:
